test_title: PYST 56: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The image formed by a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm is real, inverted, and enlarged in size as compared to the size of the object. Which of the following is true about the position of the object?

options.text: The object is placed at 20 cm from the pole of the mirror.
The object is placed at 10 cm from the pole of the mirror.
The object is placed between 20 cm and 40 cm from the pole of the mirror.
The object is placed at 40 cm from the pole of the mirror.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The object is placed between 20 cm and 40 cm from the pole of the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an inwardly curved reflecting surface. The nature of the image formed depends on the distance of the object from the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• In this problem, the **focal length (f)** is given as **20 cm**. The **center of curvature (C)**, which is the point at a distance of **radius of curvature (R)**, is calculated as **R = 2f**. Thus, **C** is at **40 cm** from the pole.
 
• For a concave mirror to produce a **real, inverted, and enlarged** image, the object must be positioned between the **principal focus (F)** and the **center of curvature (C)**. 
 
• Since **F** is at **20 cm** and **C** is at **40 cm**, the object must be placed at a distance greater than **20 cm** but less than **40 cm**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• If the object is placed at exactly **20 cm** (at **F**), the reflected rays become parallel, and the image is formed at **infinity**, being highly enlarged. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• If the object is placed at **10 cm** (between **P** and **F**), the image formed is **virtual, erect, and enlarged** behind the mirror. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• If the object is placed at **40 cm** (at **C**), the image formed is **real, inverted**, and of the **same size** as the object, located at **C**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• **At Infinity:** The image is formed at the **focus (F)**. It is **real, inverted**, and **highly diminished** (point-sized).
 
• **Beyond C:** When the object is beyond **40 cm**, the image is formed between **F and C**. It is **real, inverted**, and **diminished**.
 
• **At C:** When the object is at **40 cm**, the image is formed at **C**. It is **real, inverted**, and **same size**.
 
• **Between F and C:** When the object is between **20 cm and 40 cm**, the image is formed beyond **C**. It is **real, inverted**, and **enlarged**.
 
• **At F:** When the object is at **20 cm**, the image is formed at **infinity**. It is **real, inverted**, and **highly enlarged**.
 
• **Between P and F:** When the object is within **20 cm**, the image is **virtual, erect**, and **enlarged**.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula and Magnification:**
 
 
• The relationship between object distance (**u**), image distance (**v**), and focal length (**f**) is given by the mirror formula: **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, expressed as **m = h'/h = -v/u**.
 
• For a **real and inverted** image, the magnification is **negative**. If the image is **enlarged**, the absolute value of **m** is **greater than 1**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the focal length of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, while that of a **convex mirror** is **positive**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual Image:** A **real image** can be obtained on a screen because the light rays actually intersect. A **virtual image** cannot be obtained on a screen as the rays only appear to diverge from a point.
 
• **Common Applications:** Concave mirrors are used in **reflecting telescopes**, **shaving mirrors** to see an enlarged view of the face, and by **dentists** to see enlarged images of teeth. They are also used in **headlights of vehicles** and **searchlights** to obtain powerful parallel beams of light when the source is kept at the **focus**.
